name: ADF (Islamic State Central Africa) insurgency in Ituri and North Kivu
started: 2019-04-01 (approximate: Islamic State began claiming ADF attacks in 2019; the ADF has been active since the 1990s)
summary: The Islamic State-affiliated ADF carries out the deadliest massacres of civilians in eastern DR Congo, killing with machetes and guns in Beni, Lubero, Irumu and Mambasa, and in 2026 pushed north into Haut-Uele for the first time in 15 years. ACLED counted at least 1,370 ADF-linked deaths in 2025, more than the M23 war, and 149 civilians killed in Ituri in May 2026 alone. It matters because the fighting has merged with the Ebola outbreak in Ituri.

sides.name: DRC and Uganda
sides.strength: Uganda had about 5,000 troops in the region by Feb 2025 (Wikipedia).

sides.name: Allied Democratic Forces / Islamic State Central Africa Province (ISCAP)

background: The ADF began as a Ugandan Islamist rebel group in the 1990s and moved into the forests around Beni. It pledged to the Islamic State, which brands it Islamic State Central Africa Province. Since late 2021 Uganda's army has fought it inside the DRC under Operation Shujaa, taking its main Madina and Apakwang camps in July 2025, but the operation scattered fighters into undefended areas, which raised attacks on civilians.

The ADF's method is terror: roadblocks before massacres, fighters disguised as soldiers or Wazalendo, attacks on hospitals and churches, and abductions for labour and recruitment. Why it matters: it is the deadliest killer of civilians in eastern Congo, and Washington's focus on M23 leaves this front comparatively neglected.
year: ADF killed 19 civilians at Mukondo (13 Oct 2025), at least 17 to 29 at Byambwe/Biambe hospital in Lubero (14-15 Nov 2025) and at least 50 at Matoto and Makoko (20 Nov). In 2026 it killed at least 16 in Lubero villages (2 Jan), 25 in Ituri (25 Jan), 66 in Irumu territory (8 Feb), at least 43 in Mambasa (2 Apr), 26-40 in Ituri and North Kivu (7 May), 20 in Beni territory (31 May), 10-30 near Beni (3 June) and 13 at Banana Ecole near Mambasa (8 Aug). Congolese and Ugandan forces freed at least 200 captives along the Epulu river (20 Apr). On 30 Apr the ADF clashed with Congolese forces at Suka na Mboka in Haut-Uele, about 50 km north of Ituri, near the Kibali gold mine. From 15 May an Ebola (Bundibugyo) outbreak in Ituri became the deadliest in DRC history (2,325+ deaths by 17 Aug), with mobs burning health facilities in Irumu and Djugu.
situation: As of late October 2026 the ADF remains active in Beni and Lubero territories and has shifted weight north into Irumu and Mambasa (Ituri) and toward Haut-Uele. UPDF-FARDC operations continue but have not stopped massacres. Ebola transmission is rising again in North Kivu (Bloomberg via CTP), complicating both security and humanitarian operations.
technical: Massacre method: roadblocks on main roads, then killings of trapped civilians with machetes and knives, sometimes beheadings; burning of homes and health centres (Wikipedia; ACLED).
Disguise: fighters pose as soldiers, security officers or Wazalendo to gain access (Wikipedia).
Drones used for surveillance in most ADF camps; an attempted drone-delivered IED in Aug 2024 failed (Wikipedia).
Fragmentation: ADF splits into small groups to avoid military positions after Operation Shujaa pressure (Wikipedia).

Geographic shift: 149 civilian deaths in Ituri in May 2026 equalled the Jan-Apr total; Irumu and Mambasa are hotspots; first ADF violence in Haut-Uele in 15 years (Suka na Mboka, 30 Apr 2026) (ACLED).
Hospitals targeted: Byambwe/Biambe health centre in Lubero (Nov 2025).
Operation Shujaa: UPDF-FARDC strikes on Madina camp from 6 July 2025; Apakwang camp, holding 1,000-1,500 fighters and dependants, claimed on 10 July 2025, but most fighters escaped (Wikipedia).
Hostage-holding: joint forces freed at least 200 civilians along the Epulu river on 20 Apr 2026.
Local politics: civil society in Baswagha chiefdom, Lubero, accused the UPLC militia of supporting the ADF (ACLED).
casualties: ACLED: at least 1,370 ADF-linked fatalities in 2025; Long War Journal: at least 967 civilians killed by the ADF in 2025 (both via Wikipedia). ACLED: 149 civilian deaths from ADF attacks in Ituri in May 2026. Incident totals Nov 2025-Aug 2026 in the sources exceed 400. Separately, CODECO killed at least 69 in Ituri on 9 May 2026.
displaced: No current figures retrieved; ADF attacks routinely empty villages (e.g. Suka na Mboka, Haut-Uele, Apr 2026).

timeline.event: ADF kills 19 civilians at Mukondo, North Kivu.
ADF attack on Byambwe hospital, Lubero, kills at least 17.
At least 50 civilians killed at Matoto and Makoko.
ADF kills at least 43 in Mambasa, Ituri.
Congolese and Ugandan forces free 200+ ADF captives along the Epulu river.
ADF clashes with FARDC at Suka na Mboka, Haut-Uele.
ADF kills 13 at Banana Ecole near Mambasa.

outlook: Watch the ADF's northward drift toward Haut-Uele and the Kibali mine, any change in Ugandan force posture, and the interaction of ADF attacks with the Ebola response in Ituri and North Kivu.
